section: International climate initiatives - UNFCCC, Kyoto Protocol, CDM, Paris Agreement, key COP outcomes, IPCC assessment reports
subsections: Special Report on Global Warming of 1.5 C - time window, pathways, 2030 CO2 cut, net-zero timing

accepted.s: At COP26, India advocated which formulation regarding unabated coal power?
accepted.x: India advocated a phase-down, rather than a phase-out, of unabated coal power at COP26.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the closely related terms ‘phase-down’ and ‘phase-out’.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India's positions in recent climate negotiations:
1. India declined to join the Global Methane Pledge.
2. India joined the Tropical Forest Forever Facility as an observer at COP30.
3. India became a full capital-contributing member of the Tropical Forest Forever Facility at COP30.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: India declined the Global Methane Pledge and joined the Tropical Forest Forever Facility as an observer. It did not become a full capital-contributing member according to the stated position.
accepted.tq: Find the incorrect membership-status statement.

accepted.s: India called for a dedicated agenda on developed-country finance obligations at which forum?
accepted.x: India called for a dedicated agenda on developed-country finance obligations at Bonn SB64.
accepted.tq: Match the demand with the forum where it was raised.

accepted.s: India's position regarding the NCQG was that the core target of US$300 billion per year was:
o: More than sufficient for developing countries
accepted.x: India criticised the US$300 billion annual NCQG target as inadequate.
accepted.tq: Use the stated evaluation of the finance target rather than its amount alone.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the change concerning India's proposed hosting of COP33?
o: India announced the bid at COP26 and confirmed it at COP30.
India announced the bid at COP28 and withdrew it in April 2026 after reviewing its commitments for 2028.
India announced and withdrew the bid at COP29.
India withdrew the bid before COP28 was held.
accepted.x: The Prime Minister announced India's bid for COP33 at COP28 on 1 December 2023; it was withdrawn in April 2026 after a review of commitments for 2028.
accepted.tq: Track the announcement and withdrawal as a two-event sequence.

accepted.s: The national statement of India at COP30 was delivered on 17 November 2025 by the:
accepted.x: India's COP30 National Statement was delivered on 17 November 2025 by the Union Environment Minister.
accepted.tq: Identify the office-holder associated with the official statement.

accepted.s: The earlier climate-finance goal that remained a major focus at COP26 was:
accepted.x: The earlier goal was to mobilise US$100 billion annually, and it was a major focus at COP26.
accepted.tq: Separate the earlier finance goal from the later NCQG target.

accepted.s:
With reference to the Loss and Damage Fund, arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Operationalisation of the Fund
B. Agreement to establish the Fund
C. Opening of the Fund to applications
D. End of the World Bank’s interim-host period
accepted.x: The Fund was agreed at COP27 in 2022, operationalised at COP28 in 2023, opened to applications at COP30, and the World Bank’s interim role extends until COP33 in 2028.
accepted.tq: Start with the agreement and then place operationalisation, applications and the terminal year.

accepted.s: The Loss and Damage Fund was agreed at COP27 and operationalised at:
accepted.x: The Fund was agreed at COP27 in 2022 and operationalised at COP28 in 2023.
accepted.tq: Distinguish establishment from operationalisation.

accepted.s: Which institution serves as the interim host and trustee of the Loss and Damage Fund?
accepted.x: The World Bank is the interim host and trustee of the Fund for four years, until COP33 in 2028.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘who performs this function?’ institutional trap.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Board of the Loss and Damage Fund:
1. It has 26 members.
2. It consists of 14 members from developing countries and 12 from developed countries.
3. It takes decisions by majority vote only.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Board has 26 members, including 14 from developing countries and 12 from developed countries. It decides by consensus, so statement 3 is incorrect.
accepted.tq: Locate the wrong decision-making method after verifying the composition.

accepted.s: The Loss and Damage Fund covers losses arising from:
o: Both economic and non-economic losses from sudden- and slow-onset events
accepted.x: The Fund covers economic and non-economic losses resulting from both sudden-onset and slow-onset events.
accepted.tq: Check both dimensions of the coverage instead of accepting an ‘only’ statement.

accepted.s: Which statement correctly describes the start-up phase of the Loss and Damage Fund?
o: It is financed exclusively by the World Bank.
It operates under the Barbados Implementation Modalities, and capitalisation remains small.
It has no application process until COP33.
It operates under the Kyoto Implementation Modalities and is fully capitalised.
accepted.x: The start-up phase is under the Barbados Implementation Modalities. The Fund was opened to applications at COP30, but its capitalisation remains small.
accepted.tq: Match the fund with its stated implementation framework and current limitation.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the two finance figures associated with the NCQG adopted at COP29?
o: US$300 billion per year by 2035 from developed countries, and a wider call for US$1.3 trillion per year from all sources by 2035
US$1.3 trillion per year by 2030 from developed countries, and US$300 billion from all sources by 2035
US$300 billion in total by 2035 from all countries, with no wider finance call
US$100 billion per year by 2035 from developed countries, and US$300 billion from all sources by 2030
accepted.x: COP29 set a core mobilisation goal of US$300 billion annually by 2035 for developed countries and made a wider call for US$1.3 trillion annually from all sources by 2035.
accepted.tq: Separate the core target, its contributor group and the wider finance call.

accepted.s: The NCQG was adopted at COP29 held in:
accepted.x: COP29 was held in Baku in November 2024, where the NCQG figures were finalised.
accepted.tq: Use the location-year pairing to distinguish successive COP outcomes.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the outcome on Article 6 at COP29:
1. Rules for Article 6.2 were finalised.
2. Rules for Article 6.4 were finalised.
3. Article 6.4 establishes the Paris Agreement Crediting Mechanism under UN supervision.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: COP29 finalised rules for Article 6.2 and Article 6.4. Article 6.4 provides for the UN-supervised Paris Agreement Crediting Mechanism, or PACM.
accepted.tq: Use the all-correct combination after checking each Article 6 component.

accepted.s: The Paris Agreement Crediting Mechanism finalised under Article 6.4 is intended to replace the:
accepted.x: The UN-supervised Paris Agreement Crediting Mechanism under Article 6.4 is intended to replace the Clean Development Mechanism.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the new Paris mechanism from the earlier Kyoto mechanism.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: COP30 was described as the ‘COP of Implementation’ and also as the ‘COP of Truth’.
accepted.tq: Start from the distinctive conference title and reject unrelated labels.

accepted.s: The outcome package of COP30 was known as the:
accepted.x: The COP30 outcome was called the Belém Political Package and was framed in a ‘mutirão’ spirit.
accepted.tq: Match the outcome document with the host city.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about COP30 outcomes:
1. The outcome was framed in a ‘mutirão’ spirit.
2. COP30 identified six thematic axes.
3. The Baku-to-Belém Roadmap concerned mobilisation of US$1.3 trillion.
4. The Tropical Forest Forever Facility was associated with US$125 billion.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements correctly describe the COP30 outcome package and its associated thematic and financial initiatives.
accepted.tq: Verify each independent COP30 outcome before selecting the complete combination.

accepted.s: At COP30, the agreed adaptation-finance outcome was to:
o: Fix adaptation finance only for developed countries
accepted.x: COP30 agreed to at least triple adaptation finance.
accepted.tq: Identify the direction and minimum scale of the finance commitment.

accepted.s: How many voluntary indicators were associated with the Global Goal on Adaptation at COP30?
accepted.x: COP30 associated 59 voluntary indicators with the Global Goal on Adaptation.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact quantitative detail rather than the nearby finance figures.

accepted.s: The Belem 4x pledge refers to quadrupling sustainable fuels by:
accepted.x: The Belem 4x pledge aims to quadruple sustainable fuels by 2035.
accepted.tq: Link the pledge name to its target year and action.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is a stated feature of NDC 3.0?
o: It is economy-wide, covers all gases and is intended to align with 1.5°C.
It applies only to developed countries.
It is limited to carbon dioxide alone.
accepted.x: NDC 3.0 calls for economy-wide, all-gas pledges aligned with the 1.5°C objective and due for COP30.
accepted.tq: Test the scope of the pledge by checking economy-wide and all-gas coverage.

accepted.s: India's new NDC target mentioned for 2035 is a reduction in emissions intensity of:
accepted.x: India's new NDC targets a 47% reduction in emissions intensity by 2035.
accepted.tq: Separate the precise percentage from nearby round-number distractors.

accepted.s: Global climate finance was estimated at US$1.9 trillion in 2023. Developing countries excluding China received approximately:
accepted.x: Developing countries excluding China received approximately 15% of global climate finance in 2023.
accepted.tq: Use the percentage-share comparison rather than the total finance figure.

accepted.s: The Special Report on Global Warming of 1.5°C was released in:
accepted.x: The Special Report on Global Warming of 1.5°C was released in October 2018.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the special report’s release date from the AR6 dates.
accepted.sec: Special Report on Global Warming of 1.5 C - time window, pathways, 2030 CO2 cut, net-zero timing

accepted.s: According to the Special Report on Global Warming of 1.5°C, warming at the then-current rate was likely to reach 1.5°C between:
accepted.x: The report projected that warming would likely reach 1.5°C between 2030 and 2052 at the then-current rate.
accepted.tq: Recall the stated time window as a paired-year range.
accepted.sec: Special Report on Global Warming of 1.5 C - time window, pathways, 2030 CO2 cut, net-zero timing

accepted.s: Pathways limiting warming to 1.5°C require global net human-caused CO2 emissions by 2030 to be approximately:
accepted.x: The pathways require approximately a 45% reduction from 2010 levels by 2030.
accepted.tq: Check both the percentage and the baseline year.
accepted.sec: Special Report on Global Warming of 1.5 C - time window, pathways, 2030 CO2 cut, net-zero timing

accepted.s: The Special Report indicated that global net-zero CO2 emissions should be reached around:
accepted.x: The report’s 1.5°C pathways require global net-zero CO2 emissions around 2050.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the net-zero date from the 2030 reduction milestone.
accepted.sec: Special Report on Global Warming of 1.5 C - time window, pathways, 2030 CO2 cut, net-zero timing

accepted.s: Which approach is inconsistent with the mitigation pathways described for limiting warming to 1.5°C?
accepted.x: The pathways require cuts that are deep, rapid and sustained; gradual or limited cuts are not sufficient.
accepted.tq: Find the option that reverses the required characteristics of mitigation.
accepted.sec: Special Report on Global Warming of 1.5 C - time window, pathways, 2030 CO2 cut, net-zero timing

accepted.s: The Climate Change 2023: Synthesis Report was released on:
accepted.x: The Climate Change 2023: Synthesis Report was released on 20 March 2023 and closed the AR6 cycle.
accepted.tq: Match the report title with its exact release date.
accepted.sec: Special Report on Global Warming of 1.5 C - time window, pathways, 2030 CO2 cut, net-zero timing

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the findings of the AR6 Synthesis Report:
1. Human influence has unequivocally warmed the climate.
2. Global surface temperature for 2011–2020 was already about 1.1°C above the pre-industrial level.
3. Greenhouse-gas emissions were at their highest level in human history.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are findings associated with the AR6 Synthesis Report.
accepted.tq: Verify the evidence statements individually before choosing the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Special Report on Global Warming of 1.5 C - time window, pathways, 2030 CO2 cut, net-zero timing

accepted.s: Without immediate, deep emission cuts, the 1.5°C threshold is likely to be crossed in the:
accepted.x: The AR6 assessment states that the 1.5°C threshold is likely to be crossed in the early 2030s without immediate, deep cuts.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the near-term threshold crossing from the longer net-zero horizon.
accepted.sec: Special Report on Global Warming of 1.5 C - time window, pathways, 2030 CO2 cut, net-zero timing

accepted.s: Which of the following combinations correctly represents the mitigation pathway described in the AR6 assessment?
o: Emissions peak before 2025; net zero by mid-century; renewables provide 70–85% of global electricity by 2050
Emissions peak in 2025; net zero by 2030; renewables provide 100% of electricity by 2040
Emissions peak before 2020; net zero by 2040; renewables provide 40–50% by 2050
Emissions peak after 2035; net zero by 2070; renewables below 30% of electricity by 2050
accepted.x: The stated pathway requires global emissions to peak before 2025, reach net zero by mid-century, and obtain 70–85% of electricity from renewables by 2050.
accepted.tq: Check all three linked milestones—peak, net zero and renewable electricity share.
accepted.sec: Special Report on Global Warming of 1.5 C - time window, pathways, 2030 CO2 cut, net-zero timing

accepted.s: For a 50% chance of limiting warming to 1.5°C, the remaining carbon budget from 2020 was assessed at approximately:
accepted.x: AR6 Working Group I placed the remaining carbon budget for a 50% chance of limiting warming to 1.5°C at about 500 GtCO2 from 2020.
accepted.tq: Recall the quantitative carbon-budget estimate and its probability condition.
accepted.sec: Special Report on Global Warming of 1.5 C - time window, pathways, 2030 CO2 cut, net-zero timing

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (AR6 contribution)
a. Working Group I
a. Working Group II
c. Working Group III
d. Synthesis Report

List-II (Title)
i. Climate Change 2022: Mitigation of Climate Change
ii. Climate Change 2023: Synthesis Report
iii. Climate Change 2021: The Physical Science Basis
iv. Climate Change 2022: Impacts, Adaptation and Vulnerability

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Working Group I corresponds to the Physical Science Basis; Working Group II to Impacts, Adaptation and Vulnerability; Working Group III to Mitigation; and the final report is the Synthesis Report.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure title pair and eliminate codes with mismatched report themes.
